View and edit completed climbing sessions.

**Routes:**

* `/dashboard` — recent sessions + toggle All
* `/sessions` — full session list

Date
Session duration
Quick view of number of climbs and difficulty range
A way to open each session to view all details and edit/update

## Prototype

**Entry:** Dashboard → **Start climbing session**

**Routes:**

* `/sessions/create` → `/sessions/[id]/active` — active session builder
* `/sessions/[id]` — completed session view

**Local web:** http://localhost:8081/dashboard

**Scenarios:** http://localhost:8081/scenarios (ROKJ-16 section)

**Mock behaviour:**

* Date/start time auto-filled (editable)
* Location from home gym; inline add if none
* Sort/filter/search climbs; add/edit climbs with attempts, tags, media placeholders
* End session: private default; public requires username
* Share session/climb shows mock copy banner

comments.body:
Review: <custom data-type="status" data-id="id-0">not approved</custom>  
Please address:  

|  | **Summary** | **Description** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | ‘Happy path’ scenario | Expected happy path to be a user with profile already fully set up |
| 2 | Need a scenario where it’s a new user  | To show what it would look like when no added climbing sessions yet |
| 3 | When profile isn’t fully set up  | user must still be able to start a climbing session and just prompt when something crucial is missing |
| 5 | Adding a location in the climbing log doesn’t work | After typing something in location name and clicking ‘add location now' nothing happens. Should be similar journey to the member profile for searching, adding a nickname and adding difficulty levels |
| 6 | Location is not required for a climbing log |  |
| 7 | **Please assume standards set on other Jira tickets are the default unless difference is requested specifically** | e.g. on <custom data-type="smartlink" data-id="id-1">https://satsumya.atlassian.net/browse/ROKJ-15</custom> “Required and optional field communication: Use an \* for required fields and don’t mention optional as that is already implied“ |
| 8 | End time usability | Make it a dropdown that you can choose to type in or select from options |
| 9 | Avoid telling people to go elsewhere to edit a field if they could update it when it’s relevent | e.g. Instead of saying “End time will be 16:02 unless you set one above.“ put the end time/duration fields near the confirm and save session |
| 10 | Duration | Make it a dropdown that you can choose from common options e.g. 30mins, 45mins, 1hr,1.5hr,2hr etc |
| 11 | Hide the search and filter | When there’s no climbs or only one hide the search and filter |
| 12 | Save/end session | Open a bottom sheet with the private/public option and end time/duration |
| 13 | Do not specify (default) if it’s already implied | e.g. “Private (default” should just be “Private” |
| 14 | Date format | Update to “Day DD Mmm YYYY” e.g. Friday 03 Jul 2026 |
| 15 | Adding username for public session | Previously we’d made the username “thegoat” the way to test a username being attempted to being added that’s already taken but the error handling allowed the username “thegoat”. There needs to be username validation like in the profile setup |
| 16 | Return to dashboard | Allow users to go back to the dashboard if they’re in the middle of adding a climbing session without having to save/end the session (it should just save where it is especially since it’s not published yet |
| 17 | When to show share session  | Only show the option to share when a session is saved or ended |

comments.body:
**Starting Stage 1 development** alongside [ROKJ-3](https://satsumya.atlassian.net/browse/ROKJ-3).

Building member profile setup flow from acceptance criteria: location, difficulty levels (default colour sequence), optional fields, pet rock avatar placeholders, then dashboard.

Will mark criteria complete on this ticket as each item is implemented in the clickable prototype.

**Implementation complete — ready for review**

All acceptance criteria marked complete in member profile setup screen (`/profile/setup`).

**Test paths:**

1. Happy path: complete all fields including optional username/strengths
2. Alternate path: skip optional fields, still complete with required location
3. Error path: tap Complete profile without adding a location

Linked from sign up welcome flow ([ROKJ-3](https://satsumya.atlassian.net/browse/ROKJ-3)).

Added prototype test links to the ticket description, populated the **Decision tree**, and reformatted **Outcome summary** as bullets + scenario table.

Profile scenarios are also available from http://localhost:8081/scenarios (run `npm run web` first).

Review: <custom data-type="status" data-id="id-0">not approved</custom> 

Please address the following:

|  | **Summary** | **Description** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Required and optional field communication | Use an \* for required fields and don’t mention optional as that is already implied |
| 2 | Input errors | Error validation should happen in real time instead of waiting until the user tries to continue |
| 3 | Remove excess prototype text | Some text on this ticket was added for context but not needed on the prototype e.g. “Default option: cartoon pet rocks” Please remove any text that a user wouldn’t expect to see |
| 4 | Need to be able to exit member profile | Some fields are required for users to use other features but users can still exit the member profile set up if they want to |
| 5 | Username needs validation | We’ll need to check if a username is available. For testing please make ‘thegoat’ a username that’s already taken so we can view that scenario |
| 6 | 'Location name' / location | This field should be an address search with suggested addresses showing as the user types. If the user enters a location and the address can’t be found, there should be an option to add anyway  |
| 7 | Location added - encourage user to add levels | When a location is added it needs to feel more seamless to move users onto adding difficulty levels |
| 8 | Location edit | After a location is added a user needs to be able to edit the location easily if they made a mistake or need to update the location |
| 9 | Difficulty levels sort | Make it clear they are adding level from easy to hard and allow users to swap the sorting from hard to easy |
| 10 | Remove level numbers | e.g. Level 1 name should just be “Level label” |
| 11 | Changing level colours | Allow users to click on the colour to open a menu or dropdown of the default colour types or click a plus button to choose from a colour wheel with hex code available |
| 12 | Difficulty levels - removing | If a user adds too many difficulty levels they need to be able to remove a level if they want. But a user should not be able to delete the level if there’s no other levels added to the location |
| 13 | Be concise when displaying levels | Try showing levels as a row so it’s less overwhelming and easier for users to see more levels |
| 14 | Difficulty level rearranging | Users should also be able to drag the levels to a different position as well as moving with arrows |
| 15 | Locations added | Only show one location with levels at a time. e.g. an accordion for each location, only allow one location accordion open at any time |
| 16 | Home location communication | Use a symbol to show which location is the home/base instead of saying ‘home/base’ |
| 17 | Change home location | Users need to be able to change which location is considered the ‘home’ |
| 18 | Remove excess level summary text | “Current levels: Yellow (#F5D547), Blue (#4A90D9), Purple (#9B59B6), Green (#2ECC71), Orange (#E67E22), Red (#E74C3C), Black (#2C3E50), White (#ECF0F1), Pink (#FF69B4), Custom (#AAAAAA), Custom (#AAAAAA), Custom (#AAAAAA)“  
it only seems to provide a summary of the first location added not all locations added and doesn’t add any extra value |
| 19 | Level colour cannot be blank | don’t allow users to remove a colour without adding a colour |
| 20 | Strength and areas to improve | These should add tags so it’s clear when it’s been added. These tags should be able to be removed as well. Offer some recommended tags that a user can tap to add, typing should be secondary |

General feedback: please use the existing ticket fields where possible e.g. decision tree and outcome summary. I’ve moved these from comments to the ticket fields

comments.body:
**Starting Stage 1 development** (clickable Expo prototype, white-label wireframes).

Read acceptance criteria from this ticket + epic [ROKJ-1](https://satsumya.atlassian.net/browse/ROKJ-1). Assumptions for prototype:

* Email verification = mock screen (tap Continue)
* Error handling = inline messages when fields empty
* Sign up path: auth → verify email → welcome → [ROKJ-15](https://satsumya.atlassian.net/browse/ROKJ-15) profile → dashboard placeholder
* Login path: auth → dashboard placeholder
* No real auth/backend

Repo: local `Rokjam` workspace. Will update this ticket as criteria are completed.

**Implementation complete — ready for review**

All acceptance criteria marked complete. Local Expo prototype covers sign up/login journeys per ticket.

**Test paths:**

1. Welcome → Sign up → (empty submit shows errors) → fill fields → Verify email → Welcome → Profile
2. Welcome → Log in → (empty submit shows errors) → fill fields → Dashboard
3. Toggle between sign up/login links on auth screens

**Run locally:** `npm install && npm start`

Added prototype test links to the ticket description, populated the **Decision tree**, and reformatted **Outcome summary** as bullets + scenario table.

Also added `/scenarios` in the app — a scenario tester with one-click paths for happy / alternate / error flows.

Start locally with `npm run web`, then open http://localhost:8081/scenarios

Review: <custom data-type="status" data-id="id-0">not approved</custom> 

Please address the following:

|  | **Summary** | **Description** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | New user sign up default to blank input fields | New users would not have added any details please leave everything that would be expected to be blank as blank |
| 2 | Input errors | Error validation should happen in real time instead of waiting until the user tries to continue |
| 3 | Password standards | Add standards for passwords e.g. use at least one symbol etc |
| 4 | Verification code | Let’s have users enter a code instead of clicking a link in an email. For testing purposes please make code: 000000 an error and every other number combination successfully verify |
| 5 | Verification resend | If a user hasn’t received the code we’ll need a way for them to re-send the email or go back to try a different email |
| 6 | Scenario for existing user attempts to sign up instead of login | If an email is recognised for an existing user and they try and sign up we could just log them in or redirect them to login |
| 7 | Remove excess prototype text | Some text on this ticket was added for context but not needed on the prototype e.g. “Returning user enters details and lands on the dashboard.” Please remove any text that a user wouldn’t expect to see |
| 8 | Sign up welcome screen | Needs an option to close. If they don’t want to jump straight into the member profile take them to the dashboard. Dashboard should then show prompts to create member profile or directly add some details from the dashboard |
| 9 | Login with username or email | Ensure existing users can use their username or email in the input field |
| 10 | Email validation | If a user enters an email that isn’t valid e.g. doesn’t have an '@' symbol they should see an error |
| 11 | Password recovery for existing users | There needs to be an option to reset your password or recover your password |

General feedback: please use the existing ticket fields where possible e.g. decision tree and outcome summary. I’ve moved these from comments to the ticket fields

**Status check:** Wireframe is ready for review from last session.

* Status: Review
* Acceptance criteria: all marked DONE
* Decision tree + Outcome summary fields updated (review feedback from comments 10011 / 10013)
* Test: http://localhost:8081/scenarios

Jira MCP re-authenticated this session — no code changes needed on this ticket.
